headline: Trump's 'no Iran deal' and Saudi strikes lift oil 3%; Treasuries slump, gold hits 13-month low
summary: Trump's post that the US does not need an Iran deal, then Houthi strikes on Saudi oil sites, sent Brent up 3.3% and turned a quiet reopen into a heavy Treasury selloff, with the 2-year up about 14bp and the 10-year back above 5.10% after a soft 30-year auction. The dollar's push to a 19-month high and rising hike bets knocked gold about 2.8% to its lowest since October 2025 and silver 3% to near $50. Bunds and OATs gave up early gains to end a few bp higher.
drivers: Iran deal hopes fade, Saudi sites hit

Trump wrote that Washington no longer needs a deal with Iran, and the Houthis said they struck a pumping station on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, a Yanbu oil facility and an Aramco building. Brent settled +$3.06 at $95.82 and WTI +$2.21 at $88.74, shrugging off a 4.7m bbl US crude build.
Treasuries reopen with a hawkish selloff

With oil feeding inflation fears, the 2-year rose about 14bp to near 4.87% and the 10-year about 12bp to near 5.11%, a three-week high. Futures priced about an 85% chance of a 25bp December hike and 15% for 50bp, roughly double Tuesday's 50bp odds.
Soft 30-year sale and a big deficit

The $25bn 30-year bond stopped at 5.441%, a 0.4bp tail with a 2.36 bid-to-cover and dealers left 11.4%, after Tuesday's poor 10-year. October's $404bn deficit, well above a $300bn forecast, added to supply worries.

The dollar index rose about 0.3% to near 103.2, its highest since early April 2025. Comex Dec gold settled 2.9% lower at $3,885.30 and spot silver fell about 3% to near $50, despite haven demand from Nvidia's CEO turmoil.

oil.note: Dec WTI settled +$2.21 (+2.6%) at $88.74, back above its 200-day average; Brent +$3.06 at $95.82.
oil.why: Crude fell $1 in Asia on peace hopes, then reversed after Trump said the US does not need a deal with Iran, and rallied further when the Houthis claimed hits on a Saudi East-West pipeline pumping station, a Yanbu oil site and an Aramco building in Riyadh. Iran also said four tankers were hit in Hormuz, and Ukraine struck Russia's Ust-Luga port. That outweighed EIA builds of 4.7m bbl in crude, to 414.4m.
oil.outlook: Bias firmer in an $85–92 range while Saudi infrastructure and Hormuz shipping are under fire, though rising OPEC+ output and US stock builds cap rallies. A close above $90 opens $93–95; a credible Iran or Ukraine peace step would pull WTI back toward $84.
oil.watch: IEA report Fri Nov 13, Houthi and Hormuz headlines, Ukraine talks and EIA stocks Wed Nov 18.

gas.note: Dec RBOB rose 6.33¢ (+2.4%) to $2.6708, snapping a three-day slide; ULSD +1.8% to $4.2865.
gas.why: Gasoline followed crude higher on the Saudi and Hormuz attacks, its biggest one-day gain since Oct 30, even though EIA data showed a 1.8m bbl gasoline build and four-week demand of about 8.7m bpd. Diesel stocks rose 4.1m bbl. At the pump, AAA's average fell to $3.90, down 20¢ in a week and 45¢ in a month but still 83¢ above a year ago, on winter blends and weak autumn demand.
gas.outlook: Range of $2.55–2.78 with a neutral bias: crude risk supports futures while winter-grade supply and soft demand weigh. The pump average should keep easing toward $3.80–3.85 into Thanksgiving unless RBOB holds above $2.75.
gas.watch: Crude headlines, the AAA daily average and EIA gasoline stocks Wed Nov 18.

gold.note: Comex Dec settled -2.9% at $3,885.30; spot near $3,876, the lowest since October 2025.
gold.why: Higher oil after Trump's no-deal post revived inflation worries, which pushed Treasury yields up 12–14bp and the dollar index to near 103.2, its highest since April 2025. Futures moved to about 85% odds of a 25bp December hike and 15% for 50bp, raising the cost of holding bullion. Gold ignored haven demand from Nvidia's CEO exit and fell for a third day, down about 5.5% over three sessions.
gold.outlook: Bias lower in a $3,820–3,950 range while real yields and the dollar climb; a close below $3,850 opens about $3,800. A soft PPI or a dollar pullback would bring $3,950–4,000 back.
gold.watch: US PPI Fri Nov 13, Fed speakers, the dollar and Nvidia earnings Tue Nov 17.

silver.note: Spot fell about 3% to near $50.0 after testing below $50; it gave back Wednesday's 1.5% bounce.
silver.why: Silver fell harder than gold as the same mix of higher yields, a 19-month-high dollar and growing Fed hike bets met worries over industrial demand. The Nvidia CEO resignation hit chip and AI data-centre stocks, a key source of silver demand, and tighter financial conditions weighed on the wider metals complex. Spot touched its lowest since Nov 4.
silver.outlook: Bias lower in a $48.5–52 range while yields rise; a daily close below $49.5 would retest the October lows. A soft PPI and a rebound in chip stocks would bring $52 back.
silver.watch: US PPI Nov 13, chip stocks, copper and Nvidia results Nov 17.

us2y.note: Up about 14bp to near 4.87%, a four-week high, as hike bets built on the reopen.
us2y.why: The front end led the selloff after Trump's no-deal post lifted oil and inflation fears, catching up on two days of moves after Wednesday's holiday. Fed funds futures moved to about 85% odds of a 25bp December hike and 15% for 50bp, roughly double Tuesday's 50bp odds. Jobless claims rose 9,000 to 200,000, still too low to argue for a pause.
us2y.outlook: Bias higher in a 4.78–4.95% range while oil and Fed speakers push hikes; a firm PPI would target 4.95%. A soft PPI or a peace step that drops oil would pull it back toward 4.78%.
us2y.watch: PPI Fri Nov 13, Fed speakers and the Dec 8–9 FOMC.

us5y.note: Up about 14bp to near 4.97%, a three-week high, with the belly leading the early selling.
us5y.why: The 5-year is where extra hikes bite hardest, and it opened lower as traders priced a longer cycle after the oil jump. A short-lived bounce on Nvidia's CEO exit failed well before Tuesday's levels. Existing home sales fell 5.5% to a 3.75m rate, the lowest since August 2010, which showed higher rates are hurting but did not slow the selling.
us5y.outlook: Range of 4.88–5.05% with an upward bias; a firm PPI would open 5.05%, while a soft one or an oil drop would bring 4.88%.
us5y.watch: PPI Fri Nov 13 and Fed speakers.

us10y.note: Up about 12bp to near 5.11%, above its 50-day average and at a three-week high.
us10y.why: Trump's comment that no Iran deal is needed added an oil premium to inflation risk, and the 10-year moved above 5.10% after a soft 30-year auction in the afternoon. October's $404bn budget deficit, against a $300bn forecast, added to supply worries after Tuesday's poor 10-year sale. Haven buying on Nvidia's CEO turmoil only briefly held yields near 4.99% early.
us10y.outlook: Bias higher in a 5.02–5.20% range while oil stays firm and hikes are priced; above 5.20% opens October's highs near 5.3%. A soft PPI or an Iran peace step would bring 5.02%.
us10y.watch: PPI Fri Nov 13, oil and Nvidia earnings Tue Nov 17.

us30y.note: Up about 10bp to near 5.45% after the 30-year sale tailed at 5.441%.
us30y.why: The $25bn 30-year auction stopped at 5.441%, 0.4bp above the when-issued level, the widest tail since June, with a 2.36 bid-to-cover and dealers left 11.4% versus 6.8% last month. Coming after Tuesday's weak 10-year sale and a $404bn monthly deficit, it showed buyers still demand more for long duration. The curve flattened as the 2-year rose more on hike bets.
us30y.outlook: Range of 5.38–5.52% with a mild upward bias on supply and hikes; a break above 5.52% would need a hot PPI. A soft PPI and lower oil would bring 5.38%.
us30y.watch: PPI Fri Nov 13 and next week's 20-year auction.

de2y.note: Up about 3bp to near 3.15%, reversing an early dip as oil jumped on Trump's Iran comments.
de2y.why: Short Bunds fell about 1–2bp in the morning as markets took a breather after Tuesday's US-led rise, then turned higher when Trump's no-deal post lifted oil and US yields. Higher energy prices support the case for the ECB's December hike, which is close to fully priced after Lane and Nagel backed it. The 2-year is on track for a weekly rise of about 13bp.
de2y.outlook: Range of 3.08–3.22% with a slight upward bias while oil stays firm and a December hike is priced; an Iran or Ukraine peace step that drops oil is the main downside trigger.
de2y.watch: Euro-area GDP Fri Nov 13, ECB speakers and the Dec 17 meeting.

de5y.note: Roughly flat near 3.16%, early gains lost as Treasuries sold off.
de5y.why: The belly rallied in the morning on calm after Tuesday's spillover, then gave the gains back as Brent jumped above $95 and the Treasury selloff accelerated in early US trade. European cash markets closed before the soft US 30-year auction pushed US yields to session highs, so Bunds missed part of the move and may catch up on Friday.
de5y.outlook: Range of 3.08–3.24% with a mild upward bias; a 10-year Treasury above 5.20% would lift it to 3.24%, while a peace-driven oil drop would bring 3.08%.
de5y.watch: Euro-area GDP and US PPI Fri Nov 13.

de10y.note: Up about 3bp to near 3.33–3.36% after trading as low as 3.29% in the morning.
de10y.why: The benchmark fell 2bp early as investors paused after the week's US inflation shock, then turned higher after Trump said no Iran deal is needed, oil rose and Treasuries sold off; Dow Jones had it 1.3bp higher at 3.327% by midmorning New York. It is set for a weekly rise of about 5bp after four weeks of declines.
de10y.outlook: Range of 3.26–3.42% with an upward bias while US yields climb; a 10-year Treasury above 5.20% or hawkish ECB news would push it above 3.42%. A peace step that drops oil would bring 3.26%.
de10y.watch: Euro-area GDP and Fitch's Germany review Fri Nov 13; US PPI.

de30y.note: Up about 2bp to near 3.71%, lagging the 2-year as the curve flattened.
de30y.why: The long end followed US yields higher once oil jumped, but rose less than the front end because the move was driven by hike bets rather than supply. Wednesday's soft long Bund sale still hangs over the market, and German issuance for defence and infrastructure keeps term premium elevated. The soft US 30-year auction came after European markets closed.
de30y.outlook: Range of 3.64–3.78% with a mild upward bias on supply; a break above 3.78% would need US 30-year yields above 5.5% or another weak German auction.
de30y.watch: US PPI Fri Nov 13 and next week's German supply.

fr2y.note: Up about 5bp to near 3.68%, the biggest rise on the French curve.
fr2y.why: Short OATs track ECB pricing, and the oil jump after Trump's no-deal post and the US selloff firmed bets on a December hike, with Lane and Nagel already on board. ECB Governing Council member Vujcic said France needs a credible fiscal adjustment, a rare named warning that kept French paper under pressure.
fr2y.outlook: Range of 3.60–3.75% with a slight upward bias while ECB hike pricing firms; a lasting oil drop that cools inflation is the main downside trigger.
fr2y.watch: French final CPI Fri Nov 13, ECB speakers and the ECB Dec 17.

fr5y.note: Up about 1bp near 4.25–4.28%, steadier than the short end.
fr5y.why: Middle OATs were pulled between higher ECB hike pricing at the front and a stable French risk premium. Vujcic's call for a credible French fiscal adjustment was a reminder that ECB help is conditional, but the spread to Germany barely moved, and the move followed Bunds and Treasuries rather than French politics.
fr5y.outlook: Range of 4.15–4.33% with a neutral bias; budget progress would pull it toward 4.15%, while a government crisis or hawkish ECB surprise would lift it toward 4.33%.
fr5y.watch: French final CPI Nov 13 and the Senate budget debate.

fr10y.note: Up about 1–2bp to near 4.80–4.84%; spread to Bunds near 148bp, little changed.
fr10y.why: OATs opened near 4.79% with the spread at about 148bp and followed Bunds higher once oil jumped and Treasuries sold off. ECB's Vujcic singled out France as needing a credible fiscal adjustment, and ING sees about 150bp as a floor for the spread through the pre-election period, so the risk premium stays sticky even as Moody's kept France at Aa3.
fr10y.outlook: Range of 4.72–4.92% with the spread held near 140–158bp; a budget passed even by decree could tighten it toward 140bp, while a government crisis would push it above 160bp.
fr10y.watch: French final CPI Nov 13, the Senate budget debate and the Dec 9 Senate vote.

fr30y.note: Up about 3bp to near 5.39%, with the long end following global duration selling.
fr30y.why: Long OATs fell with Treasuries and Bunds after the oil jump on Trump's Iran comments, as investors priced higher long-run inflation and policy rates. Fiscal warnings from the ECB's Vujcic and heavy US long-end supply added to the reluctance to hold duration, though the 10s30s curve barely moved.
fr30y.outlook: Range of 5.30–5.48% with a mild upward bias; a credible budget path could take it toward 5.30%, while a political setback or US 30-year yields above 5.5% would lift it toward 5.48%.
fr30y.watch: Senate budget debate, US PPI Fri Nov 13 and rating reviews.

watch: Next: US PPI, euro-area GDP, French final CPI and the IEA oil report Fri Nov 13; Nvidia earnings Tue Nov 17; then the Fed Dec 8–9 and ECB Dec 17.
